rationale: Round-3 duty: judge whether 3f35e4e3 honestly anchors the hook's nil-contract, and re-sweep for any other empty-Phase-contract consumer the arm-value change touches. ANCHORING: yes — ReadState now checks phase.BeadsDirMissing(root) BEFORE ever calling phase.ResolveContext (internal/hook/hook.go, new early return). That is the on-disk predicate itself (a single os.Stat on root/.beads, the same exported implementation derive.go and run.go use — one predicate, no drifting copy, never bd error text), not a value side-effect of derivation. The contract runPreCommit documents ('st == nil -> mindspec not initialized, allow') previously held only by accident: pre-bead-5, the WorktreeMain arm left Phase "" on the no-.beads error, and ReadState's `hs.Mode == "" && hs.SessionStartedAt == ""` sentinel collapsed that to nil. Bead 5's honest-idle arm (a deliberate, disclosed improvement for instruct/state-show) changed that arm's value "" -> "idle", silently re-routing the sentinel and flipping bootstrap-time protected-branch commits from allow to block. The fix moves the contract onto its real precondition, which is exactly what my lens would ask for: a consumer whose behavior encodes 'is this workspace initialized' now asks that question directly of the disk rather than inferring it from a sentinel another layer happens to emit. Both halves are pinned by the new internal/hook/readstate_test.go: nil for a no-.beads workspace (red if the early return is reverted, since the arm now derives "idle"), AND a non-nil ModeIdle state for an initialized, healthy, zero-active-spec workspace — the second test matters because it proves the fix did not over-correct by swallowing the genuine idle case, whose protected-branch block is designed behavior ('ANY mode (including idle)'). I also verified the early return's session-info drop is harmless: hook.Run dispatches ONLY 'pre-commit' to a stateFn-consuming handler (every other name returns Pass), and runPreCommit reads only the nil-check, Mode, and ActiveWorktree — no consumer of session-only HookState exists. RE-SWEEP for other ""-vs-idle sentinel consumers of the changed arm: the complete set of Phase comparison sites outside internal/phase (from my round-2 grep, re-confirmed) is instruct_tail.go:30, run.go:161/183, and cleanup.go:50. cleanup treats "" and ModeIdle IDENTICALLY (both non-blocking: `Phase != ModeIdle && Phase != ""`), so the "" -> "idle" change cannot alter its outcome; instruct_tail and run.go are the arm's intended beneficiaries (uninitialized renders honest idle, and pre-bead-5 they rendered idle for "" anyway, so user-visible output is unchanged there); guard.go and resolve/target.go never read Phase (SpecID stays "" on this arm, so no redirect/target change). No remaining consumer distinguishes the two values — the fix misses nothing. AUDIT HONESTY, on my own round-2 verdict: my round-2 sweep asserted 'every branch's Phase value now matches pre-bead-5 semantics', which was true for the FAILURE-path values my round-1 finding concerned but overlooked this arm's deliberate "" -> "idle" change on the SUCCESS-shaped honest-idle path — I traced Phase-value stability where DerivationFailed is set, not where it deliberately is not. G1's hard block caught a consumer class (empty-Phase-as-uninitialized-sentinel) my enumeration read as outcome-unchanged because I evaluated hook dispatch only under bd-outage shapes, not the no-.beads bootstrap shape. The closed-form check above (all three comparison sites + the one nil-sentinel consumer, each traced under BOTH shapes) is what my round-2 sweep should have been; it now comes up empty. Tests: internal/hook, internal/phase, internal/instruct pass in the bead worktree; the round-2 G2 de-vacuated TestVerbOutput_Next and both new ReadState tests pass (MINDSPEC_ALLOW_MAIN=1 needed only for my environment's global pre-commit hook, the same artifact as prior rounds). Worktree left byte-identical.

findings.title: Nil-contract anchored on the on-disk predicate; both directions pinned; no other sentinel consumer remains
findings.detail: ReadState's early `phase.BeadsDirMissing(root)` return sits pre-resolution, uses the single shared os.Stat predicate (never bd error text), and is pinned in both directions (nil when uninitialized; non-nil idle when initialized-healthy, preserving the designed idle block on protected branches). runPreCommit is ReadState's only production consumer (hook.Run dispatches only 'pre-commit'), so the dropped session-only fields have no downstream reader. The full set of empty-Phase comparison sites (instruct_tail.go:30, run.go:161/183, cleanup.go:50) was re-traced under both the bd-outage and no-.beads shapes: cleanup treats "" and "idle" identically, the instruct sites are the arm's intended beneficiaries, and guard/target never read Phase. Nothing else distinguishes the changed values.

findings.title: Self-audit: my round-2 'values pre-bead-5-identical' claim missed the honest-idle arm G1 caught
findings.detail: Recorded for the tally's audit trail: round-2 R3 swept Phase-value stability only along DerivationFailed paths and declared every branch pre-bead-5-identical; the WorktreeMain no-.beads arm's deliberate "" -> "idle" change (a disclosed bead-5 feature, not a failure path) also moved a value under a sentinel consumer — hook.ReadState's nil contract — which round-2 G1 caught and 3f35e4e3 correctly fixes at the predicate level. The closed-form re-sweep in this round's rationale covers both shapes and comes up empty, so I assess the consumer surface as fully accounted for at this commit.
